# Install locations of known implants: MicrosoftSystem64 (related DPRK malware,
# Contagious Interview) and, below, files of PolinRider's own later stages.
# Existence of any of these is a confirmed compromise, not a signal to weigh.
#
# The implant is a Node.js Single Executable Application: a native binary with
# the V8 engine and the JavaScript payload statically linked in. It does not
# need Node installed, and it sets its own process title to look like a system
# service. Endpoint tooling that expects either a native executable or an
# interpreted script tends to miss it.
#
# Sources: safedep.io MicrosoftSystem64 binary analysis; JFrog Security Research
# "Hugging Face as a malware CDN" (js-logger-pack), both April-May 2026.
#
# "~" is expanded to the user's home directory. Windows paths are checked by
# Windows only.

# --- install locations
~/.local/share/MicrosoftSystem64
~/Library/Application Support/MicrosoftSystem64
%LOCALAPPDATA%\MicrosoftSystem64
%LOCALAPPDATA%\MicrosoftSystem64.exe

# --- working directories written by the implant
~/.pcl-data
~/.pcl-state

# --- persistence
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.launchkeeper.MicrosoftSystem64.plist
~/.config/systemd/user/MicrosoftSystem64.service
~/.config/autostart/MicrosoftSystem64.desktop
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bablu.helper.plist

# --- dropped payloads seen on Linux and macOS
/tmp/0001.dat
/tmp/tmp7A863DD1.tmp

# --- the Python stealer's lock file on Windows, beside the Linux and macOS path
# already listed above. ~/.node_modules (the private npm prefix the stage-4
# script installs axios into) and /tmp/.pip (its fallback pip target) are
# deliberately absent: both are paths a developer could plausibly create, and
# this file is INFECTED tier with no weaker path tier to put them in.
# Source: SafeDep, "PolinRider Switches to Ethereum C2 in 30+ Repositories",
# September 2026.
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\tmp7A863DD1.tmp

# --- the same agent under a new name. The pino-ulid dropper installs the
# MicrosoftSystem64 agent's persistence as `pkg-agent`. Only the LaunchAgent is
# carried: com.launchkeeper is the MicrosoftSystem64 family's own reverse-DNS
# prefix, already in the MicrosoftSystem64 plist above.
# ~/.config/systemd/user/pkg-agent.service and
# ~/.config/autostart/pkg-agent.desktop are deliberately absent -- `pkg-agent`
# is a name a legitimate tool could use, and this file is INFECTED tier.
# Source: OpenSSF malicious-packages MAL-2026-16154 (`pino-ulid`; Amazon
# Inspector, SafeDep), September 2026.
# See docs-site/src/content/docs/indicator-reviews/2026-10-19.md.
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.launchkeeper.pkg-agent.plist

# --- persistence through npm, written by the /0x/npm-migrate stage of the
# November 2026 loaders: a runner that refetches the loader, its configuration
# (the C2 addresses), its pid and its error log. Every npm command restarts the
# runner from the snippet appended to npm's lib/cli.js, which the npm
# program-file check reads. The 2026-10-05 entry left ~/.node_modules itself
# out as a directory a developer could create; these are files inside it that
# nothing else writes.
# Sources: Greenflagged, "@adminide-stack npm compromise", 2026-11-03, updated
# 2026-11-04 (all four); GitGuardian, "GhostAction Crosses Paths With
# PolinRider: Inside the October Escalation", 2026-10-27 (the first three);
# Abnormal AI, 2026-11-12 (~/.node_modules/.npm-ws*).
# See docs-site/src/content/docs/indicator-reviews/2026-11-16.md.
~/.node_modules/.npm-ws-runner.js
~/.node_modules/.npm-ws.json
~/.node_modules/.npm-ws.pid
~/.node_modules/.npm-ws.log
